Twelve comments

Bonapart’s retreat

Although listed as a reel, this tune is in fact a set dance.
I believe at least part of it is played (by Brendan Gleeson?) in the film “Cold Mountain”, which is set in the American Civil War.
This version submitted is from Henrik Norbeck’s collection.
Trevor

↳ Posted by fidicen on January 9th, 2004.

Bonaparte’s Retreat

I can confirm that Brendan Gleeson played it. The well-known actor (Gangs of New York etc) got the part because he let it be known he could “scratch about on the fiddle”. In fact, he has been playing the fiddle since he was 17, and researched the music for the film in some detail. For more info do a Google search on “Brendan Gleeson” AND fiddle.
Trevor

↳ Posted by fidicen on January 9th, 2004.

Bonaparte’s Retreat - Brendan Gleeson

As far as I can remember, Brendan Gleeson is the only film actor I have seen who can play the fiddle/violin well enough to perform live on screen (as opposed to real musicians who have a walk-on part as themselves). What you usually see in a film is an actor who obviously can’t play, or even knows how to hold the instrument and bow convincingly, “miming” to the sound of a pro violinist off screen.
Trevor

Bonaparte’s Retreat, X:5

Here’s the A major hornpipe setting labeled “Bonaparte’s Defeat” in O’Neill’s (tune #902 in the 1001), with grace notes and dotting trimmed out. There’s also a set dance setting in D, #980, which I’ll post shortly.

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on May 29th, 2021.

Bonaparte’s Retreat, X:6

And here’s the low D set dance setting from O’Neills 1001, tune #980. The version in the 1850 is different still…

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on May 29th, 2021.

Bonaparte’s Retreat, X:7

Here’s the setting from O’Neill’s 1850, #1789. It’s notated there in E minor, but most of the Cs are sharpened so I’ve switched it to dorian to simplify the setting (and removed the dotting).

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on May 29th, 2021.
